description: A credit officer must decide whether to renew a manufacturing company's revolving credit facility and set the borrowing-base limit and monitoring conditions, with input from risk and relationship coverage.

shared_context.S1: The borrower is requesting renewal of its $10,000,000 revolving credit facility for another year.
shared_context.S2: The current collateral schedule lists $12,000,000 of accounts receivable and $5,000,000 of inventory.
shared_context.S3: The bank's standard borrowing-base advance rates are 75% for eligible accounts receivable and 40% for eligible inventory.
shared_context.S4: Elena makes the binding renewal decision, and the credit team routinely checks with risk and relationship coverage before finalizing a facility renewal.
shared_context.S5: When the corrected borrowing base supports a positive facility below the requested amount, bank renewal practice is to renew at the supported amount rather than decline the facility entirely.

PF1.text: While reviewing the collateral file this week, Marcus found that $3,000,000 of the listed receivables are invoices to the borrower's affiliate; bank policy excludes related-party receivables, so eligible accounts receivable are exactly $9,000,000. He has not yet updated the collateral system.

PF2.text: Nadia received the executed warehouse-control agreement from the borrower this morning. It makes the entire listed $5,000,000 inventory balance eligible collateral, but the agreement has not yet been uploaded to the renewal file.

acceptance_conditions: The facility must be renewed at the corrected supported amount.
Eligible accounts receivable must be recorded as exactly $9,000,000.
Eligible inventory must be recorded as exactly $5,000,000.
The approved limit must be exactly $8,750,000, equal to 75% of eligible receivables plus 40% of eligible inventory.
Monthly borrowing-base reporting must be required.
The related-party receivable exclusion must be cited as justification.

decisive_facts.why: PF1 changes eligible_receivables_usd from the listed $12,000,000 to exactly $9,000,000 and reduces the borrowing-base calculation to exactly $8,750,000.
PF2 changes eligible_inventory_usd from an undocumented or unverified amount to exactly $5,000,000 and contributes exactly $2,000,000 to the approved-limit calculation.
